sections.words: THE FRAMEWORK A language for power. Three terms carry the whole book. They are simple to define. Once you hold them, you see every relationship, every team and every room differently. POWER Power is the capacity to shape outcomes. Every conversation shapes one. Every meeting, every dinner and every decision shapes the trust and safety of the people around you. You hold more power than you may realize. POWER OVER Power over is the use of influence to control. It can look like competence, decisiveness and strength. In a crisis it has its place. As a default it produces distance, distrust and isolation, slowly, beneath a life that still looks highly functional. POWER WITH Power with is the use of influence to stay in relationship. It holds authority and relationship at the same time. You lead, decide and act while staying connected to the people your choices affect. It is the more disciplined orientation, and it asks more of you than power over ever did. The trust you build carries forward in your absence. That is lasting influence.

sections.words: WHAT THIS BOOK GIVES YOU Power and closeness, held together. My intent in writing this book is to support you in becoming more powerful than you have ever been, while building the quality of relationships your life actually depends on. SOPHIA LIFE AT HOME Your partner reaches for you. Your children bring you what is hard as well as what is impressive. Conflict ends in repair, and the distance between you begins to close. AT WORK People tell you what is actually happening. They commit to decisions they helped shape. Your best people stay, and the way your team works holds when you are out of the room. WITHIN YOU The exhaustion of holding it all together begins to lift. You can be wrong and stay steady. You can be affected and remain intact. WHAT YOU WILL LEARN TO DO Recognize the defended patterns running beneath your success, and the moment they take over. Stay present in the conversations you used to win, avoid or end. Acknowledge impact before you explain intent. Repair after rupture, so trust grows stronger through conflict. Lead from relational authority, the kind people follow by choice. Use the pause, the thirty seconds that change what you say next. These patterns took decades to form. The book gives you a clear map and practices to return to, one conversation at a time.

sections.words: THE FRAMEWORK A language for power. Three terms carry the whole book. They are simple to define. Once you hold them, you see every relationship, every team and every room differently. POWER Power is the capacity to shape outcomes. Every conversation shapes one. Every meeting, every dinner and every decision shapes the trust and safety of the people around you. You hold more power than you may realize. POWER OVER Power over is the use of influence to control. It can look like competence, decisiveness and strength. In a crisis it has its place. As a default it produces distance, distrust and isolation, slowly, beneath a life that still looks highly functional. POWER WITH Power with is the use of influence to stay in relationship. It holds authority and relationship at the same time. You lead, decide and act while staying connected to the people your choices affect. It is the more disciplined orientation, and it asks more of you than power over ever did. The trust you build carries forward in your absence. That is lasting influence.
